threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to Dalston Junction and not just call it the 'Dalston' station like the locals do.
Caught a night bus home from the Elephant, and a bloke was serenading us with 90s R&B. Only in Bermondsey, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a man making a coffee from an old bike under the overpass, it hit me—this is home. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a Döner while waiting for an evening U-Bahn, with street musicians serenading the chaos. It's the perfect blend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from here if they can name all the taco trucks on 24th without thinking. The newcomers just hit up the trendy spots.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy using the Muni rail as his personal stage, belting out 80s ballads. Crowd clapped, a moment of joy amid the usual chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the best paella is found in Sitges. Meanwhile, the locals know it's just a cheap plate of rice in Gràcia that hits the spot.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a menu in English at local cafés, completely missing the vibe of the Catalan chatter around them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can catch a tube home late on a strike night. Everyone else is walking, but you’re out here waiting for a bus that’ll never come.
Last night on the 59, a guy spilled his drink and tried to mop it up with a burger wrapper. Didn't even blink when the driver shouted at him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the kids playing football in the street, while the café next door served espresso to their parents. Just another Saturday afternoon.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a converted factory that serves homemade cakes alongside rotating art exhibits. It's a slice of local creativity.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they instinctively know to dodge the BART delays but still complain about the 14 bus being late.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with a guy playing a saxophone in the back. The driver didn’t even bat an eye—just another Tuesday in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the best vibes are in the narrow streets where locals actually live and hang out.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they stand at the metro entrance, staring at the map like it’s a lost treasure map.
